sentences.text: Modern science places Anoplosaurus within the armored dinosaur group Ankylosauria, specifically in the class Ornithischia.
This quadrupedal herbivore had a low body posture and stood roughly 1.70 meters tall while reaching a total length of about 5.00 meters.
Estimates suggest the animal weighed approximately 2500 kilograms.
Harry Govier Seeley created the genus name in 1879, choosing a title meaning "unarmed" because the original bones lacked visible armor plates.
The initial material consisted of a partial skeleton with jaw pieces, many back bones, shoulder parts, leg bones, ribs, and other fragments from the Cambridge Greensand Formation.
Later researchers designated a right shoulder blade as the official type specimen to represent the species.
The dinosaur belongs to the superfamily Ankylosauria, the family Nodosauridae, and the subfamily Struthiosaurinae.
Scientists identify it as a distinct taxon closely related to Silvisaurus condrayi and Texasetes pleurohalio.
Anoplosaurus inhabited Europe during the Middle Cretaceous, specifically within the Cenomanian stage between 100.5 and 93.9 million years ago.
A second species, Anoplosaurus major, is now thought to be a chimera formed by mixing a neck vertebra from an ankylosaur with tail vertebrae from an indeterminate iguanodont.
Regarding the species Anoplosaurus curtonotus, experts Pereda-Suberbiola and Barrett proposed that its missing armor resulted from the animal dying at a very young age.
